name: GA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Sanford Bishop holds a large fundraising edge ($1.36M raised, $431K on hand) over Matt Day ($218K raised, no cash on hand)
District leans Democratic (PVI D+4) and the national environment adds to the fundamentals
Prediction markets price Bishop's reelection at roughly 97%
No public polls or expert ratings, so the outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: Bishop combines incumbency, a dominant money advantage, and a district that leans Democratic, while markets price his reelection near-certain and the challenger has no cash on hand. The evidence points to a comfortable hold, with uncertainty only about the size of the margin.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Bishop or a sharp shift in the national environment could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Sanford Bishop, a longtime Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in Georgia's second district, which leans Democratic by about four points on the partisan index. He faces Republican Matt Day, a first-time challenger who has raised roughly $218,000 and reports no cash on hand, while Bishop has raised about $1.36 million and holds more than $430,000.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets give Bishop roughly a 97% chance of winning, and his financial and incumbency advantages align with the district's lean. The forecast expects Bishop to win comfortably, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
